title: Why do animals attack?
text: Many people think that wild animals attack because they are evil. In fact, animals almost never attack without a reason. Scientists say that most attacks have one of three causes: fear, hunger or protection.

Fear is the most common cause. If an animal feels trapped, it will defend itself. A snake usually tries to escape, but if you step on it, it will bite. That is why experts say: if you see a snake, stay calm and walk away slowly.

Hunger is another reason. When there is not enough food in nature, some predators come closer to towns. If a bear finds food in your rubbish, it will come back again and again. In some national parks, visitors have to keep their food in special boxes.

Protection is the third reason. Mothers protect their babies very strongly. A hippo looks slow and peaceful, but if you get between a mother and her baby, she will attack. Hippos kill more people in Africa than lions do.
The good news is that we can avoid most attacks. If we respect the space of wild animals, they will usually leave us alone. Remember: we are visitors in their home.

grammar.title: Grammar: the first conditional
grammar.rule: Use the first conditional for a possible situation and its result: If + present simple, will + verb.
rows: If you step on it, it will bite.
If a bear finds food, it will come back.
If you stay calm, you will be safe.
It will not attack if you walk away.
